an advanced synthetic eddy model is proposed and systematically optimised for the computation of three-dimensional turbulent aerofoil noise.
an advanced method to generate flow turbulence has been developed and applied to aerofoil– turbulence interaction noise.

the development of a new SEM, which is able to generate a realistic turbulent eddy field with the correct velocity spectra.
the development of a reliable and efficient method to simulate aerofoil–flow interaction noise, which is of great importance in the field of aircraft engine design.
the development and optimisation of a synthetic eddy method, which is then combined with the sponge-layer technique to generate a realistic three-dimensional turbulence field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a promising candidate for the simulation of aeroacoustic noise in complex flow fields.
the present approach is an advanced SEM that is able to generate realistic turbulent eddies with a high degree of freedom and flexibility in its parametrisation.
the proposed SEM can be considered to be a reliable tool for the computation of the aerodynamic sound generated by aerofoil–vortex interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, with the proposed SEM, it is now possible to directly compute sound waves from the turbulent source mechanism without the necessity of using an artificial noise source.

, with the proposed SEM, it is possible to generate a realistic turbulence field in an arbitrary domain section and, with the sponge-layer technique, to quietly inject the synthetic eddies into a computational domain without disturbing the flow and the generated sound waves.
the SEM can be used as an advanced method to generate realistic flow turbulence, which is particularly suitable for the aeroacoustic simulation of complex flow problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SEM can be a powerful tool to generate realistic turbulent eddies and thus to investigate aeroacoustic problems with a complex flow field.
the SEM can be used as a reliable and efficient method to generate a realistic turbulence field for aerofoil–noise simulations.
